## INTRODUCTION - ENGINE  [939005234]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > INTRODUCTION - ENGINE
- Kind: repair procedure (removal / refitting, operation number = code)
- Applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS, 3.2 JTS, 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V, 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005234

#### ATTENTION

#### WARNINGS
This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where there is no longer a traditional ignition key having been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and go) combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver.
> Note: When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn.

## 1004B10 POWER UNIT WITH MANUAL GEARBOX - R.R  [939010395]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > 1004 ENGINE AND POWER UNIT > 1004B POWER UNIT ASSEMBLY > 1004B10 POWER UNIT WITH MANUAL GEARBOX - R.R
- Kind: repair procedure (removal / refitting, operation number = code)

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Removing
- Position the vehicle on a lift.
- Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position, then disconnect the battery terminal (-).
|  | Description | Connector |
| --- | --- | --- |
| - | Battery | See A001 BATTERY [→939004879] |
Op. 0010T84 COOLANT FOR AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM - DEHYDRATE AND REPRESSURIZE [→939010380]
Op. 7210A18 R.R FRONT CROSSMEMBER [→939011413]
- Using a suitable syringe, draw off the power assisted steering fluid from the reservoir.
Op. 4130B40 SUPPLY PIPE FROM PUMP TO POWER STEERING BOX - R.R. [→939010825]
1. Loosen the band and disconnect the supply pipe from the power assisted steering fluid reservoir to the pump, power assisted steering pump side.
2. Disconnect the rapid connector for the return pipe from the heat exchanger pipe to the power assisted steering fluid reservoir, heat exchanger side.
3. Undo the bolts (3a) and remove the power assisted steering fluid reservoir (3b) complete with pipes (3c).
4. Loosen the band and disconnect the coolant return pipe, cylinder head side.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000121.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Disconnect the rapid connector for the power assisted steering system heat exchanger inlet pipe, heat exchanger side.
2. Remove the heat exchanger pipe (2a) after having released it from the securing band (2b).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000122.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Undo the bolt (1a) and disconnect the inlet/outlet pipes from the air conditioning compressor (1b).
> Note: Seal the connectors that have been disconnected using suitable plugs to prevent dampness and impurities from entering the system.
2. Undo the nut (2a) and disconnect the air conditioning pipes intermediate flange (2b).
> Note: Seal the connectors that have been disconnected using suitable plugs to prevent dampness and impurities from entering the system.
3. Remove the air condtioning system pipes.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000123.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods

- Place the power unit in its housing using the hydraulic hoist.
1. Place the gearbox side support flexible mounting (1a) in its housing and secure it tightening the bolts (1b) and the new bolts (1c) to the recommended torque.

- Connect the gear selector and engagement cables.

- Connect the coolant return pipe to the engine coolant reservoir and tighten the collar.
- Connect the rapid connectors for the air conditioning system heater coolant inlet and outlet pipes.
- Connect the electrical connections for the Lambda sensors.
- Connect the rapid connector for the fuel supply pipe, multiple connector side.
- Connect the rapid connector for the fuel vapour pipe intermediate coupling.
- Connect the brake servo vacuum intake pipe, air chamber side and tighten the band.
- Connect the electrical connection, place the junction unit in its housing and close the cover.
- Place the battery drip tray complete with injection/ignition system control unit in its housing and secure it using the bolts.
- Connect the electrical connections to the injection/ignition system control unit.
Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]
- Place the air conditioning system pipes in their housings.
- Connect the air conditioning pipes intermediate flange and tighten the nut to the recommended torque.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EXPANSION VALVE SIDE PIPE CONNECTOR | Nut | M8 | 1.8 ÷ 2.2 |  |
- Connect the air conditioning compressor inlet/outlet pipes and secure them by tightening the bolt to the recommended torque.
> Note: Replace any O-Rings for the connectors using green coloured seals only which are resistant to the R134a refrigerant fluid.Lubricate the connector threads using anti-freeze.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

- Place the heat exchanger in position and fasten it with the band.
- Connect the rapid connector for the power assisted steering system heat exchanger inlet pipe, heat exchanger side.
- Connect the coolant return pipe, cylinder head side, and tighten the band.
- Place the power assisted steering fluid reservoir complete with pipes in its housing and secure it using the bolts.
- Connect the rapid connector for the return pipe from the heat exchanger pipe to the power assisted steering fluid reservoir, heat exchanger side.
- Connect the supply pipe from the fluid reservoir to the power assisted steering pump, power assisted steering pump side, and tighten the band.

1. Undo the gearbox drain plug and collect the fluid in a suitable container.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods

2. Disconnect the rapid connector for the fuel return pipe, fuel return manifold side.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001039.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
- Draw off the power assisted steering fluid from the reservoir using a suitable syringe.
1. Disconnect the rapid connector for the power assisted steering system heat exchanger inlet pipe.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001040.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
1. Disconnect the rapid connector for the power assisted steering system heat exchanger outlet pipe.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001041.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
1. Undo the nuts (1a) and disconnect the inlet/outlet pipes from the air conditioning condenser (1b).
> Note: Seal the connectors that have been disconnected using suitable plugs to prevent dampness and impurities from entering the system.
2. Loosen the band and disconnect the air supply hose between the turbocharger and the heat exchanger, heat exchanger side.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001042.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
1. Loosen the band and disconnect the air supply hose from the heat exchanger to the rigid pipe, heat exchanger side.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001043.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
- Position a hydraulic jack underneath the engine cooling radiator.
- Undo the bolts fixing the engine cooling radiator mounting brackets to the front suspension crossmember.
- Remove the engine cooling radiator mounting brackets.
- Remove the engine cooling radiator complete with heat exchanger and air conditioning condenser.
- Open the junction unit cover.
- Release the clips and rotate the junction unit.
1. Disconnect the electrical connection (connector E) for the radiator cooling fan wiring.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
1. Undo the bolt (1a) and disconnect the inlet/outlet pipes from the air conditioning compressor (1b).
> Note: Seal the connectors that have been disconnected using suitable plugs to prevent dampness and impurities from entering the system.
2. Loosen the band and disconnect the power assisted steering pump inlet pipe, power assisted steering pump side.
3. Undo the connector and disconnect the supply pipe from the pump to the power assisted steering box, power assisted steering pump side.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001045.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
##### Refitting
- Secure the power unit using the support tools.
- Place the power unit in its housing using the hydraulic hoist.
1. Tighten the new bolts fixing the gearbox side flexible mounting to the rigid support to the specified torque.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side support flexible mounting | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | (support side) 6.3 - 7.7 + 45° |  |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001064.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Timing side power unit rigid support flexible mounting | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | (bodyshell side) 6.3 - 7.7 + 90° |  |
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Timing side power unit rigid support flexible mounting | Bolt | M10 | (bodyshell side) 5.4 - 6.6 |  |
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Timing side power unit rigid support flexible mounting | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | (rigid support side) 6.3 - 7.7 + 90° |  |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001065.jpg]

- Fasten the gear selection and engagement cables to the mounting bracket securing them using the clips.
- Connect the gear engagement cable.
- Connect the gear selector cable.
- Connect the pipe between the damper and clutch operating cylinder, operating cylinder side and secure it using the retaining clip.
- Connect the electrical connection to the reversing light switch.
- Connect the starter motor earth lead to the contact board and secure it using the nut.
- Connect the rapid connectors for the climate control system heater coolant inlet and outlet pipes.
- Place the air supply pipe from the heat exchanger to the intake manifold back in its housing and secure it using the bolt.
- Connect the air supply hose from the heat exchanger to the intake manifold, throttle body side and secure it using the bolts.
- Connect the flexible hose to the rigid coolant return pipe to the engine coolant reservoir and tighten the band.
- Connect the rapid connector for the vacuum intake pipe to the vacuum pump.
- Connect the electrical connections to the glow plug control unit.
- Connect the electrical connection to the air flow meter.
1. Connect the supply pipe from the pump to the power assisted steering box, power assisted steering pump side and tighten the connector to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Supply pipe from pump to power assisted steering box | Connector | M16 | (power assisted steering pump side) 3.6 - 4.4 |  |
2. Connect the power assisted steering pump inlet pipe, power assisted steering pump side and tighten the band.
3. Connect the air conditioning compressor inlet/outlet pipes (3a) and secure them by tightening the bolt (3b) to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| COMPRESSOR SIDE PIPE CONNECTOR | Bolt | M8x90 | 2.2 ÷ 2.6 |  |
> Note: Replace any O-Rings for the connectors using green coloured seals only which are resistant to the R134a refrigerant fluid.Lubricate the connector threads using anti-freeze.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001069.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
- Connect the electrical connection for the radiator cooling fan wiring.
- Place the junction unit in its housing and secure it using the clips.
- Close the junction unit cover.
- Place the engine cooling radiator in its housing complete with heat exchanger and air conditioning condenser using the hydraulic jack.
- Place the engine cooling radiator mounting brackets in their housings and secure them using the bolts.
- Remove the hydraulic jack from underneath the engine coolant radiator.
- Connect the air supply hose from the heat exchanger to the rigid pipe, heat exchanger side and tighten the band.
- Connect the air supply hose between the turbocharger and the heat exchanger, heat exchanger side, and tighten the band.
- Connect the air conditioning condenser inlet/outlet pipes and secure them by tightening the nuts to the recommended torque.
> Note: Replace any O-Rings for the connectors using green coloured seals only which are resistant to the R134a refrigerant fluid.Lubricate the connector threads using anti-freeze.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PIPE CONNECTOR ON CONDENSER | Nut | M8 | 1.8 ÷ 2.2 |  |
- Connect the rapid connectors for the inlet and outlet pipes to the power assisted steering system heat exchanger pipe.
- Connect the rapid connector for the fuel return pipe, fuel return manifold side.
- Connect the fuel supply pipe rapid connector, pressure pump side.
- Tighten the gearbox oil drain plug to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox oil drain plug | - | - | 1.7 (gearbox side) |  |

- Connect the fuel supply pipe rapid connector.
- Connect the fuel return pipe rapid connector.
- Tighten the nut fixing the power assisted steering fluid return pipe to the bracket.
- Fit the intake chamber and secure it using the bolts.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Air chamber | Bolt | - | 2.3 | 3.2 JTS |
- Connect the rapid connector for the fuel vapour pipe to the solenoid valve.
- Connect the electrical connection for the fuel vapour solenoid valve.
- Connect the rapid connector for the oil vapour recovery pipe to the right cylinder head.
- Connect the electrical connection for the air pressure sensor on the intake chamber.
- Connect the electrical connection for the throttle casing.
- Place the corrugated hose complete with flow meter back in its housing and tighten the bands.
- Connect the electrical connection for the flow meter.
- Connect the heater supply and return pipes.
- Connect the electrical connections for the Lambda sensors upstream of the catalytic preconverters.
- Connect and fasten the brake servo vacuum pipe using the band, intake chamber side.
- Place the engine coolant reservoir back in its housing and secure it using the nuts.
- Connect the degassing pipe to the engine coolant reservoir and fasten it using the band.
- Connect the ends of the gear selection-engagement cables to the gear selection-engagement levers.
- Fasten the gear selection-engagement cables to the reaction bracket using the retaining clips.
- Remove the peg locking the gear selector lever.
- Connect the system supply pipe using the band, pump rigid inlet pipe side.
- Connect the earth lead to the gearbox and secure it using the bolt.
- Connect the electrical connection for the reversing switch.
- Connect the clutch fluid pipe and fasten it using the clip, three-way connector side.
- Connect the starter motor supply lead and secure it using the nut.
- Place the anti-theft siren in its housing and secure it using the bolts.
- Place the power assisted steering box rigid fluid pipe in its housing and secure it to the suspension crossmember using the bolts.
- Connect the connector for the fluid supply pipe to the power steering pump.
- Connect the supply and return pipes to the air conditioning compressor and secure them using the bolt.
- Place the engine cooling radiator assembly supports in their housings and secure them using the bolts.
- Connect the lower engine coolant hose to the radiator.
- Connect the air conditioning system refrigerant pipes to the condenser using the nuts.
- Connect the upper engine coolant hose to the radiator.
- Connect the earth lead to the bodyshell and secure it using the nut.
- Place the wiring in its housing in the fuse and relay box and connect the connections.
- Connect the air conditioning coolant return pipe intermediate flanges and secure them using the nut.
- Connect the flexible pipe to the power assisted steering pump intake and secure it using the band.

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
##### Removing
1. Undo the nuts (1a) and disconnect the electrical connections (1b) from the starter motor.
|  | Description | Connector |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1b | Starter motor | See A020 STARTER MOTOR [→939003234] |

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
1. Undo the bolts (1a), (1b) and the nuts (1c) and remove the manual gearbox (1d).
> Note: Two mechanics are needed for this operation.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003430.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
1. Fit the flywheel lock.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860846000 | Counter-torque | Flywheel lock |  |
2. Unscrew the three bolts spaced at 120° securing the clutch cradle.
3. Fit the locating pin (3a) and the remaining part of tool (3b), tightening bolts (3c) into the sockets of the bolts removed previously.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1871003100 | Extractor/ fitting tool | Clutch mechanism removal | 3.2 JTS 2.4 JTD 20V |
4. Turn the tool handwheel until pins (4a) are in contact with disc (4b).
6. Undo the tool handwheel to discharge the clutch mechanism diaphragm spring.
- Remove the tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1871003100 | Extractor/ fitting tool | Clutch mechanism removal | 3.2 JTS 2.4 JTD 20V |
7. Remove the clutch tray.
- Remove the clutch plate.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003431.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
##### Refitting
1. Fit the tool locating pin into the crankshaft.
2. Refit the clutch mechanism in position.
> Note: It is not possible to replace the cltuch plate on its own. Instead the clutch plate/cradle assembly must be replaced.
> Note: When fitting the clutch plate the correct installation position is shown by the words "engine side" or "gearbox side".
> Note: Handle the clutch plate carefully. Do not touch the surfaces of the friction linings with your hands.
> Note: Clean any anti-corrosion protection or detergents from the friction surface of the clutch tray.
3. Fit the remaining part of tool (3a) for fitting the clutch device and tighten bolts (3b).
4. Turn the tool handwheel until pins (4a) are in contact with disc (4b).
5. Hand tighten the three free retaining bolts until the clutch device is packed together.
6. Undo the tool handwheel to discharge the clutch mechanism diaphragm spring.
- Remove the tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1871003100 | Extractor/ fitting tool | Clutch mechanism removal | 3.2 JTS 2.4 JTD 20V |
- Tighten the remaining clutch fixing bolts by hand.
- Gradually tighten the bolts fixing the clutch diagonally until the recommended torque is reached.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clutch drip tray | Bolt (pretreated to be replaced) | M8 | (Engine flywheel side) 2.8 | 2.4 JTD 20V |
7. Remove the flywheel lock.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860846000 | Counter-torque | Flywheel lock |  |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003432.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods

## 1004E20 ENGINE - DISMANTLE AND REASSEMBLE FOLLOWING OPERATION 1004E10 - WASH AND CHECK DISMANTLED PARTS - REFIT CYLINDER HEAD AND OIL SUMP - DOES NOT INCLUDE REPAIRS TO CYLINDER HEAD AND AUXILIARY UNIT  [939010401]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > 1004 ENGINE AND POWER UNIT > 1004E ENGINE ASSEMBLY INSPECTION AND REPAIRS > 1004E20 ENGINE - DISMANTLE AND REASSEMBLE FOLLOWING OPERATION 1004E10 - WASH AND CHECK DISMANTLED PARTS - REFIT CYLINDER HEAD AND OIL SUMP - DOES NOT INCLUDE REPAIRS TO CYLINDER HEAD AND AUXILIARY UNIT
- Kind: repair procedure (removal / refitting, operation number = code)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939010401

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Undo the bolts (1a) and remove the connecting rod caps (1b) and half-bearings (1c).
2. Remove the piston-connecting rod assemblies (2a) complete with half-bearings (2b).
3. Remove the crankshaft.
4. Remove the crankshaft half bearings (4a) and the thrust washers (4b).
- Remove the locating bushes from the cylinder block/crankcase.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003481.jpg]
> Note: Mark the connecting rod and cap and pay attention to the cylinder sequence. The breaking surfaces of the connecting rod and the cap match individually and therefore cannot be swapped or damaged. Do not exert pressure to the breaking surfaces.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Undo the engine oil duct plugs (1a) and the water duct plugs (1b).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003482.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Refitting
- Wash all the dismantled components thoroughly.
- Clean the matching surfaces between the oil sump and the panel under the crankcase and between the panel under the crankcase and the crankcase.
- Refit the threaded plugs for the water and engine oil ducts.
- Lubricate all the mechanical components with engine oil.
- Visually check that the cylinder head support surface does not have cracks or superficial grooves.

The main journal half-bearings fitted on the crankshaft have been selected for their optimum fitting clearance.
> Note: The crankshaft supplied by the Parts Dept. comes without half-bearings and the main journals and crankpins are the "normal" size; the half-bearings to be fitted must therefore be selected identifying the class of each main journal and crankpin for the new crankshaft.
The following must be determined for the selection of main journal half-bearings: the numerical code stamped on the flywheel; the paint mark, if present, next to the main journals.
Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001280.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
1 - Crankpin identification numerical code: the left number refers to the first timing side bearing; the final "N" is an insignificant code for 4 cylinder engines.
2 - Main journal identification numerical code: the first number refers to the first timing side bearing; the final "N" is an insignificant code for 4 cylinder engines.
3 - Series of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first timing side bearing
> Note: Only use the codes that relate to the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used.
For the identification of the main journal grade, refer to the numerical code for reference 2 in the key.
In the case of the example, the numbers 11111N indicate that all five bearings are Grade A (red) as indicated below.
A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 (if present) in the diagram.
In the case of the example, the number 94 (first on the left) corresponds to the dimensions 52.994 for the first timing side bearing which identifies Grade A (red); the same method should be applied for other groups of two digits for the same reference 3 (97 -95 -95 -94).
MAIN JOURNAL IDENTIFICATION
Main journal grade A (normal), diameter 59.994.60.000 mm, RED paint mark, numerical code 1 (94 00)*
Main journal grade B (normal), diameter 59.988.59.994 mm, BLUE paint mark, numerical code 2 (88 94)*
Main journal grade C (normal), diameter 59.982.59.998 mm, YELLOW paint mark, numerical code 3 (82 88)*
Main journal grade D (0.127 mm undersize), diameter 59.867.59.873 mm, BROWN paint mark, numerical code 6 (67 73)*
Main journal grade E (0.127 mm undersize), diameter 59.861.59.867 mm, GREEN paint mark, numerical code 7 (61 67)*
Main journal grade F (0.127 mm undersize), diameter 59.855.59.861 mm, BLACK paint mark, numerical code 8 (55 61)*
(*): Last two numbers (thousandth part) of the main journal dimensions.
- In the case of the usage of a crankshaft where the maximum undersize for the bearings is 0.127 mm through grindings, the grade should be selected through the measurement of the diameter of the bearing using the above as a reference.
Having defined the grade and the colour of each new or reground crankshaft bearings, it is necessary to select the thickness of the bearings that should be the same colour as the corresponding bearing; the pair of half-bearings required can be ordered from the Parts Dept. by quoting the order no.
The above is designed to guarantee the optimum operational clearances for all the bearings.
Lastly, we wish to point out that, generally, the clearance between the main journal and the half-bearing, obtained through the selection method indicated above, should be within the following values: Minimum: 0.011 mm - Maximum: 0.071 mm; this value can be measured, as a final check, using the calibrated wire (plastic gauge).
Place the upper main bearing half-bearings in their seats in the engine block.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods
##### Removing
1. Fit the tool on the crankshaft.

2. Lock the crankshaft using the tool fitted previously for undoing the (left) bolt (2a) and remove the toothed drive pulley (2b).
3. Undo the bolts (3a), (3b) and remove the crankcase front cover with the oil pump incorporated (3c) complete with intake (3d).
4. Undo the bolts and remove the support (4a) complete with moving timing belt tensioner (4b).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/199000650.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods
1. Undo the bolts (1a) and remove the connecting rod cap (1b).
2. Remove the lower connecting rod half-bearing.
3. Remove the connecting rod-piston assembly
4. Remove the upper connecting rod half-bearing.
- Carry out the same operations to remove the pistons and connecting rods for the remaining cylinders.
- Remove the tool.

| 1860815000 | Flange | Crankshaft rotation |  |

- If the value for the crankshaft endfloat does not correspond with the recommended figures, when refitting, regrind the crankcase seat and use suitable oversize thrust washers.
6. Undo the bolts (6a) and remove the bearing caps (6b).
7. Remove the lower main journal half-bearings.
8. Remove the crankshaft.
9. Remove the upper main journal half-bearings.
10. Remove the thrust washers.
11. Undo the bolts (11a) and remove the jets (11b) from the crankcase.
12. Undo the bolt (12a) and remove the rpm sensor (12b).

Op. 1028H60 SET OF PISTONS, GUDGEON PINS AND SEALS - REPLACE PISTONS AND CONNECTING RODS AT THE BENCH - INCLUDES ALIGNMENT AND BALANCING [→939010452]
Op. 1084B18 ENGINE OIL PUMP, REMOVED - CHECK AT BENCH [→939010655]
- Fit the intake duct on the oil pump and secure it using the bolts.
- Fit the crankcase on the overhaul stand and secure it using the bolts.
- Position the rpm sensor in its housing and secure it using the bolt.
- Place the jets in their housings in the crankcase and secure them using the bolts.
- Place the thrust washers in their seats on the third main bearing.
- The main journal half-bearings fitted on the crankshaft have been selected for their optimum fitting clearance.
> Note: The crankshaft supplied by the Parts Dept. comes without half-bearings and the main journals and crankpins are the "normal" size; the half-bearings to be fitted must therefore be selected identifying the class of each main journal and crankpin for the new crankshaft.
The following must be determined for the selection of main journal half-bearings:
- the numerical code stamped on the flywheel;
- the paint mark, if present, next to the main journals.
Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/199001529.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods
1 - Crankpin identification numerical code: the left number refers to the first timing side bearing; the final "N" is an insignificant code for 4 cylinder engines.
2 - Main journal identification numerical code: the first number refers to the first timing side bearing; the final "N" is an insignificant code for 4 cylinder engines.
3 - Series of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first timing side bearing.
> Note: Only use the codes that relate to the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used.
- For the identification of the main journal grade, refer to the numerical code for reference 2 in the key.
- In the case of the example, the numbers 11111N indicate that all five bearings are Grade A (red) as indicated below.
- A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 (if present) in the diagram.
In the case of the example, the number 94 (first on the left) corresponds to the dimensions 52.994 for the first timing side bearing which identifies Grade A (red); the same method should be applied for other groups of two digits for the same reference 3 (97 - 95 - 95 - 94).
MAIN JOURNAL IDENTIFICATION
- Main journal grade A (normal), diameter 59.994 - 60.000 mm, RED paint mark, numerical code 1 (94 00)*
- Main journal grade B (normal), diameter 59.987 - 59.993 mm, BLUE paint mark, numerical code 2 (87 93)*
- Main journal grade C (normal), diameter 59.982 - 59.986 mm, YELLOW paint mark, numerical code 3 (82 86)*
- Main journal grade D (0.127 mm undersize), diameter 59.867 - 59.873 mm, BROWN paint mark, numerical code 6 (67 73)*
- Main journal grade E (0.127 mm undersize), diameter 59.860 - 59.866 mm, GREEN paint mark, numerical code 7 (60 66)*
- Main journal grade F (0.127 mm undersize), diameter 59.855 - 59.859 mm, BLACK paint mark, numerical code 8 (55 59)*
- (*): Last two numbers (thousandth part) of the main journal dimensions.
- In the case of the usage of a crankshaft where the maximum undersize for the bearings is 0.127 mm through grindings, the grade should be selected through the measurement of the diameter of the bearing using the above as a reference.
- Having defined the grade and the colour of each new or reground crankshaft bearings, it is necessary to select the thickness of the bearings that should be the same colour as the corresponding bearing; the pair of half-bearings required can be ordered from the Parts Dept. by quoting the order no.
- The above is designed to guarantee the optimum operational clearances for all the bearings.
Lastly, we wish to point out that, generally, the clearance between the main journal and the half-bearing, obtained through the selection method indicated above, should be within the following values:
- Minimum: 0.025 mm - Maximum: 0.052 mm; this value can be measured, as a final check, using the calibrated wire (Plastigage).
- Place the bearing caps complete with half-bearings in their seats.
> Note: The bearing caps have progressively numbered references (from zero to four starting from the front of the engine) which define the fitting position.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/199000660.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods
1. Tighten the bearing cap bolts (1a) to the recommended torque using the angular tightening tool (1b).

> Note: The cylinder head gasket is ASTADUR type. The material from which the gasket is made undergoes a polymerization process during the operation of the engine so that it becomes considerably harder during usage. In order for the polymerization process to take place, it is necessary to:- keep the gasket sealed in its casing until it is fitted;- not lubricate the gasket or the contact surfaces with oil.

1. Undo bolts (1a) and remove crankcase rear cover (1b) with built-in oil seal.

- Check that there are no signs of seizing on the flywheel ring gear teeth; if this is not the case, replace it.
- Fit the crankcase on the overhaul stand and secure it using the bolts.
- Fit the thrust washers on the fourth bearing support.
> Note: The crankshaft supplied by the Parts Dept. comes without half-bearings and the main journals and crankpins are the "normal" size; the half-bearings to be fitted must therefore be selected identifying the class of each main journal and crankpin for the new crankshaft.
The following must be determined for the selection of main journal half-bearings:
- the numerical code stamped on the flywheel;
- the paint mark, if present, next to the main journals.
Below is an example of the identification of main journal grades.
1. - Crankpin identification numerical code: the number on the left refers to the first timing-side bearing; for 4 cylinder engines, there is an "N" in place of the number for the 5th crankpin
2. - Main journal identification numerical code: the first number on the left refers to the first timing-side bearing; for 4 cylinder engines, there is an "N" in place of the number for the 6th main journal.
3. - Series of numbers (if present), in groups of two digits, which indicate the dimensions (thousandth part) of the main journals: the first two numbers on the left refer to the first timing-side main journal.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939005619.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
> Note: Only use the codes that relate to the key, all other codes on the flywheel should not be used.
For the identification of the main journal category, refer to the numerical code for reference 2.
In the case of the example, the numbers 111111 indicate that all six bearings are Grade A (red) as indicated in the Table.
A further method for identifying the grade of the bearings is to read reference 3 (if present) in the diagram.
In the case of the example, the number 94 (first on the left) corresponds to the dimensions 59.994 for the first timing-side bearing which, as indicated in the Table, identifies Grade A (red); the same method should be applied for other groups of two digits for the same reference 3 (97 - 95 - 95 - 94 - 95).
MAIN JOURNAL IDENTIFICATION
Bearing grade A - Normal, diameter (mm) 59.994 - 60.000, paint mark -, numerical code 1 (94 00)°
Bearing grade B - Normal, diameter (mm) 59.988 - 59.994, paint mark -, numerical code 2 (88 94)°
Bearing grade C - Normal, diameter (mm) 59.982 - 59.988, paint mark -, numerical code 3 (82 88)°
Bearing grade D - Undersize, diameter (mm) 59.867 - 59.873 (*), paint mark -, numerical code 6 (67 73)°
Bearing grade E - Undersize, diameter (mm) 59.861 - 59.867 (*), paint mark -, code 7 (61 67)°
Bearing grade F - Undersize, diameter (mm) 59.855 - 59.861 (*), paint mark -, code 8 (55 61)°
(*) 0.127 mm undersize
(°) Last two numbers (thousandth part) of the main journal dimensions
In the case of using a crankshaft where the maximum undersize for the bearings is 0.127 mm through grindings, the grade should be selected through the measurement of the diameter of the bearing using the Table as a reference.
Having defined the grade and the colour of each new or reground crankshaft bearing, it is necessary to select the pair or thickness of the bearings that should be the same colour as the corresponding bearing; the pair of half-bearings required can be ordered from the Parts Dept. by quoting the order no.
The above is designed to guarantee the optimum operational clearances for all the bearings.
Lastly, we wish to point out that the clearance between the main journal and the half-bearing, obtained through the selection method indicated above, should generally be within the following values:
- Minimum: 0.025 mm - Maximum: 0.052 mm; this value can be measured, as a final check, using the calibrated wire (plastigage).

##### Refitting
- Clean the residues of sealant from the mating surfaces between the cylinder head and the engine block.
- Clean the residues of sealant from the mating surfaces between the oil sump and the engine block.
- Clean the parts removed thoroughly and check their condition visually.
- Fit the water/oil sealing plugs in the engine block using suitable fitting tools.
- Place the engine oil jets in their housings and tighten the bolts.
- Lubricate all the mechanical components with engine oil.
- Check that the cylinder head support surface does not have cracks or grooves.

## 1008A46 POWER UNIT RIGID SUPPORT - TIMING SIDE - R.R.  [939010407]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > 1008 POWER UNIT SUPPORTS > 1008A POWER UNIT FASTENINGS > 1008A46 POWER UNIT RIGID SUPPORT - TIMING SIDE - R.R.
- Kind: repair procedure (removal / refitting, operation number = code)
- Applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS, 3.2 JTS, 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V, 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939010407

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Removing
- Position the vehicle on a lift.
Op. 1048A28 VACUUM AIR CIRCUIT RESONATOR PIPE - R+R [→939010516]
- Using a suitable syringe, draw off the power assisted steering fluid from the reservoir.
1. Undo the connector (1a) and disconnect the supply pipe from the pump to the power assisted steering box (1b), power assisted steering pump side.
2. Loosen the band and disconnect the power assisted steering fluid pipe from the reservoir to the pump, power assisted steering pump side.
3. Loosen the band and disconnect the power assisted steering fluid return pipe from the heat exchanger to the reservoir, reservoir side.
4. Undo the bolts (4a) and remove the power assisted steering fluid reservoir (4b) complete with pipe (4c).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000166.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Undo the bolts (1a) and disconnect the intermediate exhaust pipe (1b), exhaust manifold side with the catalytic converter.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000167.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Undo the bolts fixing the power unit lower reaction rod, engine crankcase sump side.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000168.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Undo the bolts fixing the power unit rear support flexible mounting, rigid support side.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000169.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Support the power unit using a hydraulic hoist fitted with a suitable chain connected to the mounting bracket on the engine.
2. Undo the bolts (2a), (2b) and remove the power unit timing side front support flexible mounting (2c) complete with power assisted steering fluid reservoir mounting bracket (2d).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000170.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
- Raise the engine, as necessary, using the hydraulic hoist.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000171.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Refitting

| Timing side power unit rigid support | Bolt | M12 | (engine crankcase side) 8.5 - 10.5 | 1.9 JTS 2.2 JTS |

| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Timing side power unit rigid support flexible mounting | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | (bodyshell side) 6.3 - 7.7 + 90° |  |

## 1008B30 GEARBOX SIDE SUPPORT FLEXIBLE MOUNTING(S) - REPLACE  [939010411]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > 1008 POWER UNIT SUPPORTS > 1008B POWER UNIT SUPPORT MOUNTINGS > 1008B30 GEARBOX SIDE SUPPORT FLEXIBLE MOUNTING(S) - REPLACE
- Kind: repair procedure (removal / refitting, operation number = code)
- Applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS, 3.2 JTS, 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V, 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939010411

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Removing
- Position the vehicle on a lift.
Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]
Op. 5530B52 BATTERY SUPPORT/DRIP TRAY - R.R [→939011009]
- Position a hydraulic jack underneath the gearbox.
1. Undo the bolts fixing power unit gearbox side rigid support to the manual gearbox.
2. Undo the bolts fixing the gearbox side support flexible mounting to the bodyshell.
3. Remove the gearbox side support flexible mounting (3a), complete with rigid support (3b).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000182.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. At the bench, undo the bolts (1a) and separate the gearbox side support flexible mounting (1b) from the rigid support (1c).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000183.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Refitting
1. Assemble the gearbox side support flexible mounting (1a) and the rigid support (1b) and secure them tightening the new bolts (1c) to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side support flexible mounting | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | (support side) 6.3 - 7.7 + 45° |  |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000184.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
1. Remove the gearbox side support flexible mounting (1a), complete with rigid support (1b).
2. Tighten the bolts fixing the gearbox side support flexible mounting to the bodyshell to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side support flexible mounting | Bolt | M10 | (bodyshell side) 5.4 - 6.6 |  |
3. Tighten the new bolts fixing the power unit gearbox side support to the manual gearbox to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side power unit rigid support | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | (gearbox side) 6.3 - 7.7 + 45° |  |
- Remove the hydraulic jack from underneath the gearbox
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000185.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
Op. 5530B52 BATTERY SUPPORT/DRIP TRAY - R.R [→939011009]
Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]
- Remove the vehicle from the lift.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
##### Removing
Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]
Op. 5530B52 BATTERY SUPPORT/DRIP TRAY - R.R [→939011009]
- Position a hydraulic jack underneath the gearbox.
1. Undo the bolts (1a), (1b), then remove the power unit gearbox side support flexible mounting (1c).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001299.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
##### Refitting
1. Place the power unit gearbox side support flexible mounting (1a) in its housing and secure it tightening the bolts (1b) and the new bolts (1c) to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side support flexible mounting | Bolt | M10 | (bodyshell side) 5.4 - 6.6 |  |
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side support flexible mounting | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | (support side) 6.3 - 7.7 + 45° |  |
- Remove the hydraulic jack under the engine crankcase sump.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001300.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
Op. 5530B52 BATTERY SUPPORT/DRIP TRAY - R.R [→939011009]
Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]

> Block applies to: engines: 3.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Removing
Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]
Op. 5530B52 BATTERY SUPPORT/DRIP TRAY - R.R [→939011009]
Op. 7055B54 UNDER ENGINE PROTECTION/GUARD - R.R. [→939011369]
- Position an arm lift underneath the gearbox.
1. Undo the bolt and release the earth lead from the gearbox.
2. Undo the bolts fixing the rigid power unit support to the gearbox.
3. Undo the bolts (3a) fixing the flexible mounting to the rigid support; remove the rigid support (3b) from the gearbox.
4. Undo the bolts (4a) securing the flexible mounting (4b) to the bodyshell and remove it.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946001135.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 3.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Refitting
- Fit the flexible mounting in its housing and secure it to the bodyshell tightening the bolts to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side flexible mounting to bodyshell | Bolt | M10 | 5.4 ÷ 6.6 |  |
- Place the rigid support in its housing and secure it to the flexible mounting tightening the bolts to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side flexible mounting to support | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | 6.3 ÷ 7.7 + 45° |  |
- Tighten the bolts securing the rigid power unit support to the gearbox to the specified torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side power unit rigid support to gearbox | Bolt | M12 | 6.3 ÷ 7.7 + 45° |  |
- Connect the earth lead to the gearbox and secure it using the bolt.
- Remove the arm lift positioned underneath the gearbox.
Op. 7055B54 UNDER ENGINE PROTECTION/GUARD - R.R. [→939011369]
Op. 5530B52 BATTERY SUPPORT/DRIP TRAY - R.R [→939011009]
Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
##### Removing
Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]
Op. 5530B52 BATTERY SUPPORT/DRIP TRAY - R.R [→939011009]
- Position a hydraulic jack underneath the gearbox.
1. Undo the bolts (1a), (1b), then remove the power unit gearbox side support flexible mounting (1c).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939005631.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
##### Refitting
- Place the power unit gearbox side support flexible mounting in its housing and secure it tightening the bolts to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side support flexible mounting | Bolt | M10 | (bodyshell side) 5.4 - 6.6 |  |
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side support flexible mounting | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | (support side) 6.3 - 7.7 + 45° |  |
- Remove the hydraulic jack from beneath the gearbox

Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R+R [→939011011]

## 1008C32 GEARBOX LOWER REACTION ROD -R.R.  [939005236]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > 1008 POWER UNIT SUPPORTS > 1008C POWER UNIT REACTION ELEMENTS > 1008C32 GEARBOX LOWER REACTION ROD -R.R.
- Kind: repair procedure (removal / refitting, operation number = code)
- Applies to: engines: 3.2 JTS; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005236

##### Removing
Op. 7055B54 UNDER ENGINE PROTECTION/GUARD - R.R. [→939011369]
1. Mark the position of the two flanges connecting the rear drive idler casing to the propeller shaft.
2. Undo the bolts fixing the two flanges connecting the rear drive idler casing to the propeller shaft.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946001137.jpg]

1. Undo the fastenings securing the gearbox side lower reaction rod to the front suspension frame and to the gearbox, then remove it.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946001138.jpg]

##### Refitting
- Place the gearbox side lower reaction rod in its housing and secure it to the suspension frame and to the gearbox tightening the bolts to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side lower reaction rod to front suspension frame | Bolt (to be replaced) | M12 | 6.3 ÷ 7.7 + 60° |  |
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gearbox side lower reaction rod to gearbox | Bolt | M10 | 5.4 ÷ 6.6 |  |
- Place the propeller shaft in position ensuring that the marks made on the two flanges during the removal are aligned; fasten it to the rear drive idler casing tightening the bolts to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Propeller shaft - rear drive idler casing side | Bolt | M8 | 3.1 ÷ 3.7 | 3.2 JTS |

> Note: The bolts should be tightened in a crossover sequence as illsutrated in the diagram below.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946001139.jpg]

Op. 7055B54 UNDER ENGINE PROTECTION/GUARD - R.R. [→939011369]

4. Undo the bolts (4a) and remove the power assisted steering fluid reservoir (4b) complete with pipe (4c).
5. Loosen the band and disconnect the coolant return pipe, cylinder head side.

- Remove the cylinder head.
> Note: Two mechanics are needed for this operation.Take care to release the timing chain.
- Remove the cylinder head gasket.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Refitting
- Clean any residues of gasket from the the cylinder head - engine block matching surfaces.
- Carry out a visual inspection of the components.
- The lower cylinder head plane can be refaced if the flatness is betweeb 0.05 and 0.15 mm.
- The refacing does not have to be carried out for lower flatness values.
- The refacing is not permitted for higher flatness values.
- Before refacing it is necessary to check that the minimum depth for each combustion chamber is 12.75 mm (at the point shown in the diagram) in order to guarantee the minimum combustion chamber volume.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001301.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
- Place the cylinder head gasket in position.
> Note: The gasket should be positioned with the word "TOP" facing upwards.
- Place the cylinder head in position.
> Note: Two mechanics are needed for this operation.- Check that the centering bushes are correctly positioned.Take care to raise the timing chain.
1. Tighten the cylinder head fixing bolts to the recommended torque using the angular tightening tool.
> Note: Follow the order shown in the figure for each tightening sequence.

1. Place the inlet side camshaft phase transformer (1a) in its housing and secure it using a new bolt (1b) without tightening it.
2. If necessary, rotate the crankshaft until cylinder no. 4 is at T.D.C. in the explosion stroke; in this condition the reference (2a) on the inner part of the crankshaft pulley should be in line with the reference (2b) on the timing chain cover.
> Note: Rotate the crankshaft slowly and evenly (in the direction of rotation).
> Note: Ensure the timing chain is not stuck.
3. Fit the timing chain on the inlet side camshaft phase transformer.
> Note: The light blue mesh (3a) should be in line with the reference (3b) on the inlet side camshaft phase transformer.
4. Place the exhaust side camshaft phase transformer (4a) in its housing and secure it using a new bolt (4b) without tightening it.
> Note: Rotate the exhaust side camshaft using the hexagon until the pink mesh (4c) is in line with the reference (4d) on the exhaust side camshaft phase transformer.
> Note: Check that the timing chain is correctly fitted on the drive gear (on the crankshaft) checking that there are three chain links between the head support surface and the timing references on the phase transformers.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
> Note: If the chain remains slack, the tensioner is not in the operating position.
- Rotate the crankshaft through 720°, then place cylinder no. 4 at T.D.C. during the explosion stroke; in this condition the reference on the inner part of the crankshaft pulley should be aligned with the reference on the timing chain cover.
> Note: When the crankshaft is rotated the tensioner piston should follow the chain during the rotation stage.
- Check the timing making sure that the timing references correspond.

##### Refitting
- Clean the contact surfaces between the cylinder head and the crankcase.
COMBUSTION CHAMBER WITH THE POINT FOR MEASURING THE DEPTH SHOWN
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003933.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
- The lower cylinder head plane can be refaced if the flatness is not within the recommended values.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cylinder head lower surface flatness | 0.05 - 0.15 mm | 1.9 JTS 2.2 JTS |
- The refacing does not have to be carried out for lower flatness values.
- The refacing is not permitted for higher flatness values.
- After refacing it is necessary to check that the minimum depth for each combustion chamber is 12.75 mm (at the point shown in the diagram above) in order to guarantee the minimum combustion chamber volume.
- Check that the valves do not show signs of grooves or seizing.
- Check that the diameter of the valve stems corresponds to the recommended figures; if not, replace the worn valves.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet valve stem diameter | 5.900 - 5.940 mm | 1.9 JTS 2.2 JTS |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exhaust valve stem diameter | 5.900 - 5.940 mm | 1.9 JTS 2.2 JTS |

| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet valve head diameter | 34.95 - 35.25 mm | 1.9 JTS 2.2 JTS |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exhaust valve head diameter | 29.95 - 30.25 mm | 1.9 JTS 2.2 JTS |

| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods
1. Unscrew the connectors (1a) and (1b) and remove the pipes from the fuel manifold to the injectors (1c).
> Note: Use new pipes from the fuel manifold to the injectors when refitting.
2. Undo the nuts (2a) and remove the fuel distribution manifold (3b) complete with fuel pressure sensor and pipes (2c).
3. Manually push the clips (3a) and disconnect the pipe from the injectors to the fuel recovery manifold (3b), injector side, and remove it.
- Undo the nuts and disconnect the supply wiring from the heater plugs.
- Disconnect the coolant return pipe to the expansion tank and de-aeration system from the thermostat.
4. Undo the nuts (4a) and remove the air chamber (4b) complete with E.G.R. electrical valve (4c) and throttle body (4d).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/199000709.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods
1. Undo the bolts (1a) and remove the vacuum unit (1b) complete with O-ring.
2. Loosen the retaining band (2a) and disconnect the pipe (2b) from the thermostat to the oil heat exchanger, heat exchanger side.
3. Undo the bolts (3a) and remove the thermostat (3b) complete with pipe and sensor.
4. Remove the gasket.
5. Undo the bolt (5a) and the nut (5b) and remove the water/exhaust gas heat exchanger for the E.G.R. system (5c).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/199000710.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods

> Block applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods
1. Undo bolts (1a) and remove camshaft caps (1b).
> Note: The camshaft caps are numbered from 2 to 5, inlet side and from 6 to 9, exhaust side. The front cap, which is the same for both camshafts, is number 1.
> Note: The bolts securing the camshaft caps should be loosened in a spiral sequence, starting from the caps on the outside, in the following order: 5 - 2 - 4 - 3.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/194005182.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods

> Block applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods
##### Refitting
- Thoroughly clean the matching surfaces between the cylinder head and the engine block.
- Check that the planarity of the lower cylinder head plane is within the recommended values. If this is not the case, replace the cylinder head (the cylinder head lower plane cannot be reground).
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cylinder head lower surface flatness | 0.05 mm | 1.8 |
- Fit the cylinder head support tool and place the assembly in a vice.
- Check that the valves do not show signs of grooves or seizing.
1. Check that the width of the valve bore in the cylinder head is within the recommended values.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet valve seat width (mm) | 1.0 ÷ 1.4 | 1.8 |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exhaust valve seat width (mm) |  | 1.8 |
2. Check that the angle of the valve bore in the cylinder head is within the recommended values.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valve seat angle | 90° 30’ | 1.8 |
- If the values are not within the recommended limits, replace the cylinder head.
3. Check that the diameter of the valve head corresponds to the recommended figures.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet valve head diameter (mm) | 30.7 ÷ 30.8 | 1.8 |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exhaust valve head diameter (mm) | 27.1 ÷ 27.2 | 1.8 |
4. Check that the angle of the valve head is within the recommended values.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valve head angle | 90° 40’ | 1.8 |
5. Check that the diameter of the valve stem corresponds to the recommended figures.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet valve stem diameter (mm) | 4.955 ÷ 4.970 | 1.8 |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exhaust valve stem diameter (mm) | 4.935 ÷ 4.950 | 1.8 |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valve stem diameter oversizes (mm) | 0.075/0.150 | 1.8 |
- If the values are not within the recommended limits, replace the valves.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/194005189.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods
Op. 1016E14 VALVE GUIDES IN SINGLE CYLINDER HEAD - REPLACE DURING OP. 1016E10 [→939010422]
- Place the valves in their seats and support them using the support tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860804001 | Stand | Removing/refitting valves | 1.8 1.9 JTD 16V |
- Fit the valve guide oil seal using the tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1870894000 | Extractor | Valve guide oil seal extraction | 1.8 1.9 JTD 8V |
- Fit the springs and the shim.
- Position the lever fitted with an adaptor, compress the valve spring and fit the cotters.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860644001 | Lever | Removing/refitting valves | 1.8 1.9 JTD 16V |
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1870881000 | Chamber | Removing/refitting valves | 1.8 |
- Proceed in a similar way and fit the remaining oil seals, springs, shims and cotters.
- Undo the bolts and remove the valve support tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860804001 | Stand | Removing/refitting valves | 1.8 1.9 JTD 16V |
- Fit the mechanical tappet cups.
- Fit the inlet and exhaust side camshafts, following the position marked during the dismantling.
- Fit two new oil seals on the camshafts, having lubricated them with engine oil.
- Apply a bead of silicon sealant to the matching surfaces of the camshaft front cap.
- Place the camshaft front cap in position using the two centering bushes.
- Place the camshaft caps in position, following the progressive numbers indicated during the removal.
- Tighten to the recommended torque the bolts fixing the camshaft caps, following the spiral sequence from the inside towards the outside.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Camshaft caps | Bolt | - | 0.8 | 1.8 |
1. Use a feeler gauge to check that the valve clearance is within the specified limits with the valves closed.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet valve clearance in closed position (mm) | 0.21 ÷ 0.29 | 1.8 |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exhaust valve clearance in closed position (mm) | 0.27 ÷ 0.35 | 1.8 |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/194005190.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods
- If the tappet clearance is not within the recommended tolerance, remove the camshaft involved and replace the cups, selecting the size according to the required clearance.
> Note: The tappet cups are graded according to size and therefore the Spare Parts list should be consulted for selecting the new cup to be fitted. The code is on the cup crown.
- After fitting the new cups, repeat the procedure for checking the tappet clearance.
- Fit the timing belt inner guard and secure it using the bolts.
1. Fit tool (1a) in special splining on camshafts (1b).
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2000012000 | Template | Camshaft timing | 1.8 |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/194005191.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods
1. Place toothed driven pullies (1a) and (1b) in position.
2. Fit the tool on the toothed driven pullies.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2000012100 | Template | Camshaft timing | 1.8 |
> Note: Fit the inlet side template first and then the exhaust side one.
> Note: When the templates are fitted, check that:- the reference (a) on the exhaust-side pulley is aligned with the reference (b) on the corresponding timing template;- the pin (c) on the intake-side pulley is in the position illustrated in the diagram in relation to the reference (d) on the corresponding timing template.
- Tighten the bolts fixing the pullies to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Variable valve timing actuator | Bolt (to be replaced) | - | 6.5 + 120° + 15° | 1.8 |
3. Tighten the sealing plugs with new O-rings.
- Remove the templates used for timing.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/194005192.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods
- Place the thermostat unit in its housing complete with a new O-ring and tighten the fixing bolts.
- Place the inlet and exhaust side timing sensors in position and secure them using the bolts.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Timing sensor | Bolt | M6 | 0.6 ÷ 0.8 | 1.8 |
- Place the inlet and exhaust side phase transformer solenoid valves in position and secure them using the bolt.
- Fit the spark plugs and tighten them to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spark plugs | - | - | 2.5 | 1.8 |
- Place the engine lifting brackets in their housings and secure them using the bolts.
- Undo the fixing nuts and remove the cylinder head from the support tool.
- Remove the support tool from the vice.

## 1016E20 CYLINDER HEAD (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT, REMOVED - OVERHAUL  [939004944]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > 1016 CYLINDER HEAD/S > 1016E CYLINDER HEAD/S - VARIOUS OPERATIONS > 1016E20 CYLINDER HEAD (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT, REMOVED - OVERHAUL
- Kind: repair procedure (removal / refitting, operation number = code)
- Applies to: engines: 3.2 JTS; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004944

##### Removing
> Note: The dismantling of the left cylinder head is illustrated below, carry out the same operations for the right cylinder head.
1. Position the cylinder head in the vice using the tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860470000 | Support | Supporting cylinder head in vice |  |
2. Undo the engine coolant temperature sensor and remove it.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000313.jpg]

1. Undo the connectors (1a) for the fuel pipes (1b) connected to the fuel manifold pipe.
2. Undo the bolts (2a) and remove the pressure pump (2b) complete with pipes.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000314.jpg]

1. Undo the bolts (1a) and remove the fuel manifold pipe (1b) with injectors (1c) and electrical wiring (1d).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000315.jpg]

1. Undo the bolts (1a) and remove the camshaft caps (1b).
> Note: Mark the positionof the camshaft caps for the correct refitting.
2. Remove the camshafts.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000316.jpg]

1. Remove rockers (1a) and hydraulic tappets (1b).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000317.jpg]

1. Fit the reaction tool for supporting the valves during the removal.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860804000 | Stand | Removing/ refitting valves | 3.2 JTS |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000318.jpg]

1. Fit the cotters (1a) using the tools (1b) and (1c).
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1870881000 | Chamber | Removing/ refitting valves | 3.2 JTS |
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860644000 | Lever | Removing/ refitting valves | 3.2 JTS |
2. Remove the valve upper shim.
3. Remove the valve spring.
- Carry out the same operations for removing the remaining valves.
- Remove the tools used for dismantling the valves.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000319.jpg]

1. Remove the valve guide oil seals (1a) using the tool (1b).
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1870894000 | Extractor | Removing valve guide oil seals | 3.2 JTS |
- Remove the reaction tool for supporting the valves during the removal.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860804000 | Stand | Removing/ refitting valves | 3.2 JTS |
2. Keep the valves.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000320.jpg]

##### Refitting
- Clean any residues of the old gasket from the lower cylinder head plane.
- Check the planarity of the cylinder head lower plane.
- If the maximum difference in planarity is less than 0.05 mm, then the cylinder head lower plane does not require refacing.
- If the maximum difference in planarity is 0.05 - 0.20 mm, then the cylinder head lower plane should be refaced.
> Note: If grinding is necessary, it should be carried out on both cylinder heads.
> Note: The maximum permitted regrinding depth is 0.25 mm; if the cylinder head lower plane requires more regrinding , the cylinder head must be replaced.
- Remove valve deposits, checking the rod for scoring or signs of binding.
- Check that the diameter of the valve stem corresponds to the recommended figures.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inlet valve stem diameter (mm) | 5.955 ÷ 5.975 | 3.2 JTS |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exhaust valve stem diameter (mm) | 5.945 ÷ 5.965 | 3.2 JTS |
- Check that the length of the valve springs released is within the recommended values.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valve spring free length (mm) | 42.050 ÷ 44.850 | 3.2 JTS |
- Check that the diameter of the camshaft bearings is as specified.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Camshaft journal diameter (mm) | 26.936 ÷ 26.960 | 3.2 JTS |
> Note: The surfaces of the camshaft bearings should not show signs of wear, grooves or seizing.
- Check that the nominal camshaft cam lift is within the recommended figures.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nominal camshaft cam lift (mm) | 11 | 3.2 JTS |
> Note: The surfaces of the camshaft cams should not show signs of wear, grooves or seizing.
- Refit the camshaft caps on the cylinder head according to the position marked during the dismantling.
> Note: The camshaft caps are marked with a number starting from the timing side going toward the flywheel side (even numbers for the left cylinder head and uneven numbers for the right cylinder head) and a letter, "I" for the intake side camshaft and "E" for the exhaust side camshaft.The projections on the camshaft caps should be facing the centre of the cylinder head.
- Tighten the camshaft cap bolts to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Camshaft caps | Bolt | - | 1.0 | 3.2 JTS |
- Check that the diameter of the camshaft mounts is as specified.
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Camshaft support diameter (mm) | 27.000 ÷ 27.020 | 3.2 JTS |
| Measurement | Value | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Camshaft support diameter - timing side (mm) | 35.000 ÷ 35.020 | 3.2 JTS |
- Position the cylinder head in the vice using the tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860470000 | Support | Supporting cylinder head in vice |  |
- Place the valves in their seats and keep them in position using the support tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860804000 | Stand | Removing/ refitting valves | 3.2 JTS |
- Place the valve guide oil seals in their housings.
1. Fit the valve spring in its seat.
2. Refit the upper valve shim.
3. Place the half-cones (3a) in their housings using the tools (3b) and (3c).
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1870881000 | Chamber | Removing/ refitting valves | 3.2 JTS |
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1860644000 | Lever | Removing/ refitting valves | 3.2 JTS |
- Carry out the same operations for refitting the remaining valves.
- Remove the tools used for fitting the valves.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000321.jpg]

- Place the hydraulic tappets and rockers in their housings.
1. Place the camshafts in their housings.
2. Refit the camshaft caps on the right cylinder head according to the position marked during the dismantling.
> Note: The camshaft caps are marked with a number starting from the timing side going toward the flywheel side (even numbers for the left cylinder head and uneven numbers for the right cylinder head) and a letter, "I" for the intake side camshaft and "E" for the exhaust side camshaft.The projections on the camshaft caps should be facing the centre of the cylinder head.
3. Tighten the camshaft cap bolts to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Camshaft caps | Bolt | - | 1.0 | 3.2 JTS |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000322.jpg]

1. Place the fuel manifold pipe (1a) in its housing complete with injectors (1b) and electrical wiring (1c) and tighten the bolts (1d).
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fuel manifold pipe | Bolt | - | 1.0 | 3.2 JTS |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000323.jpg]

- Place the pressure pump in its housing complete with pipes and secure it using the bolts.
- Connect the fuel pipes to the fuel manifold and tighten the connectors.

1. Place the engine coolant temperature sensor in its housing and tighten it to the recommended torque.
| Component | Fastening | dia | Value (daNm) | Validity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Engine coolant temperature sensor | - | M12 | 2.2 |  |
2. Remove the cylinder head from the support tool.
| Tool | Description | Function | Validity |

| 1860470000 | Support | Supporting cylinder head in vice |  |
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946000324.jpg]

1. If lower surface flatness of the lower cylinder head is not within specified values, grind from the nominal head height and then fit a new gasket with the number of notches determined as described below.
- The head can be refaced by 0.1 mm if a gasket with 0 references was fitted and a new gasket with 1 reference is going to be used. The head can be refaced by 0.2 mm if a gasket with 0 references was fitted and a new gasket with 2 references is going to be used. The head can be refaced by 0.1 mm if a gasket with 1 reference was fitted and a new gasket with 2 references is going to be used.
> Note: When within limit conditions (head gasket with 2 notches before levelling), the lower head surface cannot be levelled.

##### Refitting
- Clean the matching surfaces between the crankcase sump and the cylinder block/crankcase.
- Apply silicone sealant to the oil sump side and rear surfaces.
> Note: Apply a continuous bead of sealant with no breaks.
- Position the crankcase sump in its housing together with the intake with no axial deviation.
- Tighten the bolts and the nut fixing the engine oil intake.
- Apply silicone sealant to the oil sump front surface.
> Note: Apply a continuous bead of sealant with no breaks.
- Tighten the side bolts securing the crankcase sump to the recommended torque using the wrench (to be used for the gearbox side bolts only).

2. Unscrew and remove the engine oil level sensor.
3. Undo bolts (3a) and remove buffeting bulkhead (3b).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939005642.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
##### Refitting
Fit the bulkhead and tighten the bolts fixing it to the oil sump.
Screw in the engine oil level sensor.
Fit the sump condensed engine oil return pipe connector.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Removing
1. Undo the bolts (1a) and remove the crankcase oil sump partition (1b).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/194000215.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Refitting
- Place the crankcase oil sump partition back in its housing and secure it using the bolts.

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods

## 1020D30 FLYWHEEL SIDE OIL SEAL COVER - R.R. AND REPLACE GASKETS WITH FLYWHEEL REMOVED  [939010437]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > 1020 CRANKCASE SUMP AND COVERS > 1020D OIL SEALS ON CRANKSHAFT > 1020D30 FLYWHEEL SIDE OIL SEAL COVER - R.R. AND REPLACE GASKETS WITH FLYWHEEL REMOVED

- Applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939010437

##### Removing
1. Undo the bolts (1a), (1b) and remove the flywheel side oil seal cover (1c).
> Note: Cut the sealant between the flywheel side oil seal cover and the crankcase sump.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001383.jpg]

##### Refitting
- Clean sealant residues off the flywheel side oil seal cover contact surface with the crankcase sump.
- Apply silicone sealant to the contact surface between the crankcase sump and flywheel side oil seal cover.
1. Place the flywheel side cover (1a) in its housing and secure it tightening the new bolts (1b) and bolts (1c) to the recommended torque.
> Note: When positioning the flywheel side oil seal cover, avoid significant sideways movements that could remove the sealant.

##### Removing
1. Remove the piston rings.
2. Release the pin (2a) and separate the connecting rod (2b) from the piston (2c).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003517.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Refitting
- Join the connecting rod and piston.
- Place the gudgeon pin in its housings and secure it using the circlips.

> Block applies to: engines: 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
##### Removing
1. Remove the piston rings.
2. Release the pin (2a) and separate the connecting rods (2b) from the pistons (2c).

Fit the pins and secure them using the circlips.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002425.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V; all production periods

## 1032A12 TIMING SYSTEM DRIVE CHAIN - R.R  [939010456]
- Path: Procedures > 10 ENGINE > 1032 TIMING SYSTEM > 1032A CHAIN TIMING SYSTEM > 1032A12 TIMING SYSTEM DRIVE CHAIN - R.R
- Kind: repair procedure (removal / refitting, operation number = code)

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
##### Removing
- Position the vehicle on a lift.
- Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position, then disconnect the battery terminal (-).
|  | Description | Connector |
| --- | --- | --- |
| - | Battery | See A001 BATTERY [→939004879] |
Op. 1048A28 VACUUM AIR CIRCUIT RESONATOR PIPE - R+R [→939010516]
- Using a suitable syringe, draw off the power assisted steering fluid from the reservoir.
1. Undo the connector (1a) and disconnect the supply pipe from the pump to the power assisted steering box (1b), power assisted steering pump side.
2. Loosen the band and disconnect the supply pipe from the power assisted steering fluid reservoir to the pump, power assisted steering pump side.
3. Loosen the band and disconnect the return pipe from the heat exchanger to the power assisted steering fluid reservoir, reservoir side.
4. Undo the bolts (4a) and remove the power assisted steering fluid reservoir (4b) complete with pipe (4c).
5. Loosen the band and disconnect the coolant return pipe.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000249.jpg]

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods

|  | Description | Connector |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1b | Inlet side phase transformer solenoid valve | See N092 PHASE SHIFTER SOLENOID VALVE ON INTAKE SIDE [→939004484] |

> Block applies to: engines: 1.9 JTS, 2.2 JTS; all production periods
